## Summary

When multiple provider API keys exist in the environment (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`), the `hermes model` selection UI stops showing AWS Bedrock as an available or active provider — even when Bedrock is correctly configured in `config.yaml` and working at runtime.

## Root Cause

The model picker uses `resolve_provider("auto")` for display purposes. Bedrock is last in the auto-detect chain, so any other API key present in the environment "wins" and the UI shows that provider as active instead. The config-level `model.provider: bedrock` is honoured correctly at runtime — it is purely a UI/display bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes to use AWS Bedrock: `hermes config set model.provider bedrock`
2. Have one or more other provider API keys set in `~/.hermes/.env` (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`)
3. Run `hermes model` — Bedrock does not appear in the picker
4. Restart Hermes — the active model shown in the UI reflects the wrong provider

## Expected Behavior

The model picker should respect the configured `model.provider` value from `config.yaml` for display, not re-run auto-detection against env vars.

## Actual Behavior

Bedrock vanishes from the model picker entirely. The UI shows a different provider as active. This causes users to believe Bedrock is broken or misconfigured, leading to incorrect recovery attempts.

## Workaround

Force provider and model via CLI, then do a full restart (`/new` is NOT enough — it does not reload config):

```bash
hermes config set model.provider bedrock
hermes config set model.default global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
# Then fully restart Hermes
```

Note: model IDs for AWS cross-region inference profiles require the `global.` prefix (e.g. `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`). Bare IDs return HTTP 400 in some regions (confirmed: eu-north-1).

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (June 2026)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on AWS EC2
- Provider: AWS Bedrock, region eu-north-1
- Other API keys present in env: Anthropic direct, OpenRouter

items.title: [Bug]: Discord /skill (and /skill_list) slash commands rejected as Unrecognized despite adapter registering them

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

On Discord, typing `/skill` (the autocomplete-driven skill runner registered by `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3759`) is rejected by the gateway with:

```
WARNING gateway.run: Unrecognized slash command /skill from discord — replying with unknown-command notice
```

…even though the adapter logs successful registration moments earlier:

```
INFO hermes_plugins.discord_platform.adapter: [Discord] Registered /skill command with 102 skill(s) via autocomplete
```

A related rejection also fires for `/skill_list`:

```
WARNING gateway.run: Unrecognized slash command /skill_list from discord — replying with unknown-command notice
```

User-visible effect: the only path Discord users have to browse and run installed skills via the slash UI is broken. `/skills` (plural) is the unrelated approval-toggle command, so there is no working slash-driven entry point to the skill catalog from Discord.

## Repro

1. Connect Discord gateway with skills installed (102 in my case).
2. Confirm registration in `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`:
   - `Registered /skill command with N skill(s) via autocomplete`
   - `Safely reconciled NN slash command(s)` (the `/skill` Command object is in the tree)
3. In Discord, type `/skill` and submit. (Autocomplete may or may not surface — irrelevant; the rejection is the same.)
4. Gateway logs `Unrecognized slash command /skill from discord` and Discord shows the unknown-command notice.

Same repro yields `/skill_list` rejection.

## What I verified (against `origin/main`)

- `hermes_cli/commands.py:317` — `GATEWAY_KNOWN_COMMANDS` is derived from `COMMAND_REGISTRY`. There is no `skill` (singular) entry in `COMMAND_REGISTRY`.
- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3759` — adapter registers `name="skill"` as a `discord.app_commands.Command` with autocomplete + handler `_skill_handler`. The handler is meant to resolve the chosen skill via `self._skill_lookup`, then call `_run_simple_slash(interaction, f"{cmd_key} {args}".strip())` — i.e. it should never forward the literal `/skill` to the gateway.
- The expected log line `[Discord] slash 'X' invoked by user=…` from `_run_simple_slash:3305` does **not** appear for these rejections. So the Discord adapter's `_skill_handler` callback is **not** what produced the rejection — the gateway received `/skill` through a different path.
- The two plausible paths:
  1. Discord delivered the `/skill` interaction's text payload to the gateway's plain `on_message` handler in parallel with (or instead of) firing the slash-command callback, and the gateway's text-side dispatcher tried to look up `/skill` in `GATEWAY_KNOWN_COMMANDS` and failed.
  2. The plugin-skill registration path that generates `/skill_list` (and similar) registers names that aren't reflected in `is_gateway_known_command`'s plugin lookup, so plugin-provided slashes get the same treatment.

Either way the symptom is the same: a slash command that the Discord adapter believes it owns is being rejected by the gateway-level dispatcher.

## Expected behavior

- `/skill <name> [args]` runs the chosen skill via the adapter's autocomplete handler — no gateway 'Unrecognized' warning.
- Plugin-registered slash commands (e.g. `/skill_list`) are recognized by `is_gateway_known_command` (or whatever the dispatcher consults) so they don't get the unknown-command notice.

## Environment

- Hermes commit: `7d183f649` (local working tree, 84 behind `origin/main` at the time of repro — verified the relevant code in `origin/main` matches the diagnosis)
- macOS 26.5 (arm64)
- Discord adapter connected via `ai.hermes.gateway` LaunchAgent
- Bot has Message Content Intent enabled
- 102 installed skills, slash sync reported `recreated=44 created=9 deleted=0`

## Possible fix sketches (not prescriptive)

- Make the gateway dispatcher consult the platform adapter's registered command set before falling through to the unknown-command branch.
- Or: in `is_gateway_known_command`, treat names registered by an active platform adapter (`/skill`, plugin slashes) as known.
- Or: stop forwarding slash-command interaction text into the on_message path when the adapter has a matching slash callback bound.

Happy to test a patch.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

On first launch, Hermes greets the user with a message promising it will "pick the right tools, explain the plan," etc. — but if no model/provider is configured (the most common new-user state), **every message immediately fails** with a cryptic AWS error. There is no fallback, no helpful guidance, and the error persists in the chat even after the issue is fixed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Agent fresh (no model configured)
2. Open the GUI / start a session
3. Send any message (e.g. *"Hello, Hermes. Nice to meet you."*)

## Actual Behavior

The response area shows a dark-red error:

```
API call failed after 3 retries: An error occurred (UnrecognizedClientException)
when calling the ConverseStream operation: The security token included in the
request is invalid.
```

This error:
- Is AWS/Bedrock-specific jargon — meaningless to most new users
- Gives no hint that the root cause is simply **no model being configured**
- Gives no guidance on how to fix it (e.g. "run `hermes setup` or `hermes model`")
- **Persists visibly in the chat** even after the user fixes the model config and starts a new message

## Expected Behavior

1. **Before any message is sent:** if no model is configured, show a clear inline notice — e.g. *"No model configured yet. Run `hermes setup` to get started."*
2. **On error:** surface a human-readable message like *"No model is configured. Run `hermes setup` to connect a provider."* — not a raw AWS exception.
3. **Error should not persist** in the chat thread after the user has resolved the issue and sent a new message.
4. **Fallback model for setup assistance:** Consider bundling or recommending a tiny, CPU-only local model (e.g. a small GGUF via llama.cpp) that can answer basic setup/configuration questions without requiring any subscription or API key. The welcome message sets expectations that the agent is functional — it should be, at least for setup help, out of the box.

## Why This Matters

The welcome message actively raises expectations ("I'll pick the right tools, explain my plan…") while the app is silently broken. This is a jarring first impression and likely causes many users to abandon setup before they get started. Users should not need to pay for a subscription just to get help with the initial configuration.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS (desktop GUI)
- Hermes version: current (fresh install)
- Provider attempted: AWS Bedrock (default — no credentials configured)

## Suggested Fixes (Priority Order)

1. **[Easy]** Detect missing/invalid model config at startup and show a dismissible setup banner in the UI
2. **[Easy]** Catch `UnrecognizedClientException` (and similar auth errors) and rewrite the user-facing message to plain English with a `hermes setup` call-to-action
3. **[Medium]** Clear or visually dismiss error messages from previous failed turns once a new successful response arrives
4. **[Longer-term]** Provide a zero-config fallback path (tiny local model, no GPU) so users can interact with Hermes for setup guidance before configuring a paid provider

---
*Filed via Hermes Agent on behalf of a new user — feedback collected during first-run experience.*

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

Cron job agents cannot use the `web_search` tool reliably in mainland China. Despite AnySearch being configured as the search backend and working fine when called via CLI directly, cron sessions' `web_search` calls fall through to DDGS — which times out on every request (Google, Yahoo, Yandex, Startpage all unreachable from China without VPN).

This causes cron jobs that depend on web search (daily briefing, Trump report, World Cup predictions, etc.) to fail silently or produce degraded output with no real-time data.

Log evidence from a single morning (2026-06-14):
```
cron_e30a9e526cdc: DDGS search error: operation timed out × 4 attempts
cron_fbacdbea1ada: DDGS search error × 3 attempts
cron_370cfb4ed80a: DDGS search error × 8 attempts
```

Meanwhile `anysearch_cli.py` direct calls succeed in under 3 seconds.

## Proposed Solution

In `tools/web_tools.py` (or wherever backend selection happens), when the configured `web.search_backend` is `anysearch` and DDGS is being used as a fallback, add a check: if DDGS fails 2+ consecutive times with timeout, auto-escalate to AnySearch via CLI subprocess, even if the AnySearch provider plugin was loaded after gateway startup.

Alternatively, make cron sessions respect the configured backend more aggressively — don't silently fall back to DDGS if the configured backend's provider is registered and available.

## Related

- #43883 — partial whitelist bug affecting AnySearch routing
- This is likely the same root cause but manifests more severely in cron sessions due to plugin load ordering

## Environment
- Hermes v0.16.0 (b5a457c0 + local commits)
- Config: `web.backend: anysearch`, `web.search_backend: anysearch`
- Network: mainland China, no VPN used by cron sessions
- AnySearch CLI works fine from same DGX host

items.title: [Bug] Hermes Desktop: right-sidebar file-tree refresh button disappears when cursor moves onto it
items.body:
**Description**
In the right sidebar's Filesystem panel, the refresh button is revealed when hovering the project label. Because the button relies on `peer-hover/project-label` but has no self-hover rule, it disappears as soon as the cursor leaves the label and enters the button area, making it impossible to click.

**Affected version**
Observed on builds after the `v0.16.0` release (2026-06-05). The regression was introduced by commit `d62979a6f` ("feat(desktop): composer status stack, live subagent windows, editable prompts", 2026-06-12) on `main`. The About panel may still display "0.16.0" in builds from this window because the version label was not bumped after the release tag (see commit `16beab421`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open Hermes Desktop and load any folder in the right sidebar file tree.
2. Hover the project label in the Filesystem header — the refresh button appears.
3. Move the cursor from the label toward the refresh button.
4. The refresh button vanishes before the click registers.

**Expected behavior**
The refresh button should remain visible and clickable while the cursor is over it.

**Actual behavior**
The button disappears when the cursor leaves the project-label hover zone because its visibility is tied only to `peer-hover/project-label`, not to its own hover state.

**Root cause**
In `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/index.tsx`, commit `d62979a6f` changed the header reveal from `group-hover/project-header` to `peer-hover/project-label`. The new `HEADER_ACTION_LABEL_REVEAL` constant sets `pointer-events-none opacity-0` as the base state and only reveals the refresh button via `peer-hover/project-label`. Once the cursor enters the button itself, the peer hover is lost, so the button flips back to hidden/non-interactive.

**Suggested fix**
Add self-hover rules to `HEADER_ACTION_LABEL_REVEAL` so the refresh button stays visible and interactive while hovered:

```diff
-const HEADER_ACTION_LABEL_REVEAL = `${HEADER_ACTION_CLASS} pointer-events-none opacity-0 transition-opacity focus-visible:pointer-events-auto focus-visible:opacity-100 peer-focus-visible/project-label:pointer-events-auto peer-focus-visible/project-label:opacity-100 peer-hover/project-label:pointer-events-auto peer-hover/project-label:opacity-100`
+const HEADER_ACTION_LABEL_REVEAL = `${HEADER_ACTION_CLASS} pointer-events-none opacity-0 transition-opacity hover:pointer-events-auto hover:opacity-100 focus-visible:pointer-events-auto focus-visible:opacity-100 peer-focus-visible/project-label:pointer-events-auto peer-focus-visible/project-label:opacity-100 peer-hover/project-label:pointer-events-auto peer-hover/project-label:opacity-100`
```

**Related**
- `d62979a6f` — commit that introduced the regression.
- #41153 — separate feature request for real-time file tree updates in the same sidebar.

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

Discord's interactive button views — `ExecApprovalView`, `SlashConfirmView`, `UpdatePromptView`, `ClarifyChoiceView` — hardcode their view lifetime to 300 seconds in `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`:

```python
super().__init__(timeout=300)  # 5-minute timeout
```

No config knob is exposed. Users running long-lived sessions over Discord (which is the entire point of the gateway) who step away from chat for >5 minutes return to "Prompt expired — no action taken" with a greyed-out button row, and have to issue the request again.

This bites hardest for `ExecApprovalView` — a user mentions Hermes, Hermes flags a dangerous command, the approval view goes up, the user goes to make coffee, comes back, and has to start over. The agent thread is still parked the whole time; the only thing that expired is the UI affordance.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with `approvals.mode: manual` (or hit any dangerous-command path)
2. Trigger an approval from Discord
3. Wait >5 minutes before clicking
4. Footer changes to "⏱ Prompt expired — no action taken", buttons go grey

## Expected

`approvals.discord_prompt_timeout` (seconds) configurable via `config.yaml`. Default 300s for backward compatibility. Clamp to a sane range so users don't accidentally make prompts unusable (too short) or push past Discord's 15-min interaction-token expiry (too long).

## Proposed fix

Add `_read_discord_prompt_timeout()` reading `approvals.discord_prompt_timeout` with the existing `read_raw_config()` pattern (matches `_read_dm_role_auth_guild()` next to it). Use it in the four confirmation views' `__init__`. Leave `ModelPickerView`'s 120s alone since that's a deliberate quick-pick UX.

PR with fix + tests incoming.

## Environment

- Hermes at `9b01c4d19`, Discord gateway

items.title: [Desktop] Model picker rewrites model.provider to wrong aggregator (e.g. openrouter) when a local proxy exposes same-prefix models

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

When a user has a local proxy provider (e.g. `litellm-proxy`) configured in `config.yaml`, picking a model whose name carries a `nvidia/...` prefix (e.g. `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3`) from the Desktop model picker silently rewrites `model.provider` to the first aggregator that accepts the same prefix in the static catalog — in our case `openrouter` — and overwrites `model.base_url`. Subsequent calls fail (OpenRouter has no `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3` route; its canonical m3 id is `minimax/minimax-m3`), and the user's `fallback_providers` chain then routes the request to a different model group, which the user has explicitly forbidden by policy.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `0.16.0` (current `main`)
- OS: Windows 11
- Configured providers in `config.yaml`: `cpa`, `ollama`, `litellm-proxy` (`api: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`, `key_env: HERMES_LITELLM_PROXY_KEY`), `custom:tokenrouter`, …
- Local proxy exposes `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3` and `nvidia/nim/kimi-k2.6`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a local proxy in `config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   model:
     default: MiniMax-M3
     provider: custom:tokenrouter
   providers:
     litellm-proxy:
       api: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
       key_env: HERMES_LITELLM_PROXY_KEY
   ```

2. Open Hermes Desktop, click the model picker, select `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3` (served by the local `litellm-proxy` in this scenario).
3. Make sure the picker is in "persist globally" mode (or there is no active session, which auto-persists).
4. Confirm the choice.

## Actual

`config.yaml` is rewritten to:

```yaml
model:
  default: nvidia/nim/minimax-m3
  provider: openrouter    # ← wrong; should be litellm-proxy
  base_url: ''            # ← lost
```

The Dashboard's "Main Model" line then shows `openrouter · nvidia/nim/minimax-m3`.

- OpenRouter returns 4xx for `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3` (verified via `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`: its m3 model id is `minimax/minimax-m3`, not `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3`).
- The user's `fallback_providers: [{model: nvidia/nim/kimi-k2.6, provider: litellm-proxy}]` then kicks in — a cross-model fallback they explicitly configured against in their internal "same-model-only" rule.

## Expected

The picker should attribute a model to the **configured** provider that actually serves it, not to a hard-coded aggregator inferred from a static namespace match. At minimum:

- If `providers.litellm-proxy` is configured and exposes `nvidia/nim/minimax-m3` via its `gateway model-options` payload, the picker's group label and persisted `model.provider` should be `litellm-proxy` (or whatever the gateway reports), not `openrouter`.
- Persisting via `/model X --provider Y --global` should refuse (or warn before) writing `model.provider` to a value the user has not explicitly enabled in `config.yaml`, and should not silently clear `model.base_url`.

## Root cause (best guess — please verify)

- `apps/desktop/src/components/model-picker.tsx` groups `models` by the static `_PROVIDER_MODELS` catalog (`hermes_cli/models.py`) — line 268–274 has `nvidia` with `nvidia/nemotron-...` entries, and `openrouter` happily accepts the same prefix — instead of by the runtime provider list returned by the gateway's `model-options` endpoint.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts:87` then sends `/model ${selection.model} --provider ${selection.provider} --global` where `selection.provider = provider.slug` from that catalog group, not from the user's `config.yaml`.
- The catalog fall-through assigns `nvidia/...`-prefixed models to `openrouter` whenever the user has any openrouter key configured in the environment (it just doesn't check whether `providers.openrouter.key_env` resolves locally).

## Suggested mitigations (any one of these would resolve it)

1. **Quote provider from the gateway's `model-options` payload**, falling back to the static catalog only when that endpoint reports zero providers. The gateway already knows which provider serves each model — use it.
2. **When grouping models, skip catalog providers whose `key_env` is unset in the current `config.yaml`.** This forces the picker to honestly display "this model would fail because no key is configured" instead of silently routing to a dead aggregator.
3. **Refuse `--global` writes that would change `model.provider` to a value not in the user's `providers:` map** without an explicit confirmation in the picker dialog.
4. **(Lightest possible fix)** Hard-coded blacklist in `model_normalize.py`: never reassign `nvidia/...`-prefixed models to `openrouter`; they should resolve to a configured `nvidia`-family provider (currently none in the registrar, which surfaces the bug honestly instead of hiding it behind an unreachable aggregator).

## Why I think this is a bug, not a UX preference

- The user had a working `litellm-proxy`-backed default. The picker silently changed the provider to something the user never enabled in `config.yaml`, and erased `model.base_url`.
- The silent cross-model fallback then violates the user's documented same-model-only policy.
- The Dashboard's "Main Model" line gives no warning that the displayed provider is a wrong inference, so the user only discovers the bug when they notice unrelated model output.

## Workaround (for now, until the fix lands)

Manually edit `config.yaml` after every picker-driven "persist globally" operation, or do not use the picker's persist-globally mode when picking a model served by a non-default proxy.
